text: We depend on a limited number of ocean carriers and port terminals; disruptions, strikes or congestion at key ports could delay shipments and raise our costs.
Fuel price volatility and changes to emissions regulation may increase our operating expenses, and we may be unable to pass these costs on to customers.
A breach of our shipment-tracking platform could expose customer data and interrupt operations, resulting in contractual penalties and reputational harm.
Our lead drug candidate may fail in clinical trials or may not receive regulatory approval from the FDA or comparable foreign authorities.
We rely on third-party contract manufacturers, and any shortage of raw materials or quality failure at their facilities could halt production.
We may be subject to patent litigation from competitors, and an adverse ruling could require us to pay damages or stop selling a product.
Our wafers are fabricated by a single foundry in one geographic region, and geopolitical tensions or export restrictions could interrupt our supply.
Demand for our chips is cyclical and a downturn in consumer electronics could lead to inventory write-downs and lower margins.
Our revenue is denominated largely in US dollars while a significant share of costs is incurred in other currencies, exposing us to exchange rate fluctuations.
Rising interest rates may compress our net interest margin and reduce the value of securities held in our investment portfolio.
Deterioration in commercial real estate could increase loan defaults and require us to raise our allowance for credit losses.
We must comply with capital and liquidity requirements, and tighter regulation could limit dividends and growth.
Our profitability depends on oil and natural gas prices, which have historically been volatile and are influenced by global supply decisions.
Climate legislation and carbon pricing could reduce demand for our products and increase the cost of compliance.
Operational accidents such as pipeline leaks or well blowouts could cause environmental damage, litigation and significant clean-up costs.
Consumer discretionary spending is sensitive to inflation and unemployment; weaker consumer confidence could reduce store traffic and sales.
We source most of our merchandise from overseas suppliers, and tariffs or shipping delays could raise costs and cause stock shortages.
We process large volumes of payment card data, and a security incident could lead to fines, litigation and loss of customer trust.
Our subscription revenue depends on customer retention, and increased churn or pricing pressure from larger competitors could harm growth.
An outage at our hosting providers or a ransomware attack could make our services unavailable and breach our service level commitments.
Evolving data protection rules such as GDPR may restrict how we process customer data and expose us to substantial fines.
Catastrophic events such as hurricanes and floods may produce claims exceeding our reserves and reinsurance coverage.
Low interest rates reduce investment income on our bond portfolio, while rising rates can cause unrealised losses.
If our underwriting assumptions prove inaccurate, claims could exceed expected levels and reduce our solvency ratio.
